title: Robert Pattinson cast as James Bond in next 007 movie
text:

 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage Robert Pattinson named as James Bond actor in next 007 movie
 Brendan Morrow, USA TODAY Updated Mon, 16 November 2026 at 3:08 pm UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The name's Pattinson. Robert Pattinson .
 The "Twilight" star, 40 , has officially been cast as the next James Bond , succeeding Daniel Craig and taking the mantle as one of cinema's most iconic characters. He will make his 007 debut in an upcoming, untitled Bond movie from "Dune" director Denis Villeneuve , with no release date set as of now.
 Amazon MGM Studios unveiled the casting on Instagram on Nov. 16 with a video showing Pattinson emerging as Bond as the classic 007 theme plays.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "James Bond will return," text on screen then says. An official photo was also released showing Pattinson in the role, holding a gun and wearing a tuxedo.
 "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement. "To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement." Villeneuve expressed "deep gratitude to the remarkable actors" who were considered for the role and said he is "overjoyed" to welcome Pattinson. "He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin."
 The news comes near the end of one of the biggest years of Pattinson's career. The star, who rose to fame for playing Edward Cullen in the "Twilight" movies, is coming off performances in three back-to-back, acclaimed films: "The Drama," a dark comedy that paired him with Zendaya; Christopher Nolan's epic, Oscar-tipped "The Odyssey"; and "Primetime," which saw him play "To Catch a Predator" host Chris Hansen. He'll finish off 2026 with a part in December's sci-fi epic "Dune: Part Three."
 Pattinson will be a rare actor to play two of the most iconic movie roles of all time: In 2022, he debuted as Batman in Matt Reeves' "The Batman ," a role he'll reprise in an upcoming sequel , scheduled for 2028. It was not immediately clear whether Pattinson will continue to play both Batman and Bond simultaneously. DC Studios recently installed a new president and chief creative officer, and questions have swirled about whether Pattinson's Batman series will continue beyond its upcoming second chapter.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The announcement ends years of speculation about who would take over as the famed British agent after Craig stepped away from the role with his final 007 film, 2021's "No Time to Die," which wrapped his run as the character in a definitive fashion. Craig had played Bond five times, beginning with 2006's "Casino Royale."
 The leading men in James Bond films have defined generations with their portrayals of Secret Agent 007, and the search for the next legendary character is on .
See who's starred as the iconic character, starting here with Sean Connery, who became the original cinematic Bond in the '60s.
 (MacGregor, Getty Images) American actor Barry Nelson played James Bond in the original live TV adaptation in 1954. It marked the first portrayal of Ian Fleming's legendary British Secret Service Agent James Bond on the small screen.
 (CBS Photo Archive, Getty Images) Australian actor George Lazenby took over the role of Secret Agent 007 from Sean Connery in "On Her Majesty's Secret Service."
 (Central Press, Getty Images) British actor Roger Moore played Bond in seven films from 1973 to 1985. "Live and Let Die" was his first.
 (Jack Kay, Getty Images) British actor Timothy Dalton launched his 007 career in "The Living Daylights," playing Bond from 1987 to 1989.
 (MYCHELE DANIAU, AFP via Getty Images) Irish actor Pierce Brosnan brought Bond into the new millennium, with films from 1995 to 2002.
 (Jon Kopaloff, Getty Images) British actor Daniel Craig is the most recent Bond, playing the storied character on the silver screen from 2006 to 2021.

 (MacGregor, Getty Images) That means Pattinson will be the first actor other than Craig to portray Bond in more than 25 years. Craig's predecessor, Pierce Brosnan , led four Bond flicks from 1995's "GoldenEye" to 2002's "Die Another Day."
 George Clooney reveals his 'perfect' James Bond actor choice 
 Pattinson will be the eighth actor to play Bond on the big screen. Sean Connery was the first, starting with 1962's "Dr. No" and initially continuing through 1971's "Diamonds Are Forever," though George Lazenby had a brief stint during that time in 1969's "On Her Majesty's Secret Service," and Connery later returned in 1983's "Never Say Never Again."
 British actor Robert Pattinson attends the red carpet event of "Primetime" presented in competition at the 83rd International Venice Film Festival, at Venice Lido on September 5, 2026. (Photo by Tiziana FABI / AFP via Getty Images) Roger Moore followed Connery from 1973's "Live and Let Die" to 1985's "A View to a Kill," and Timothy Dalton stepped in for a pair of films, 1987's "The Living Daylights" and 1989's "Licence to Kill," followed by Brosnan and Craig. David Niven also played Bond in 1967's "Casino Royale," a spoof not produced by the same company as the other Bond movies and not considered part of the series.

 Connery and Moore are tied for the record with seven Bond films each.
 The next Bond film will be the series' 26th entry, but the first produced since Amazon MGM Studios took creative control of the franchise in 2025. Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli, longtime Bond producers, have stepped back, with Wilson saying it was "time for our trusted partner, Amazon MGM Studios, to lead James Bond into the future." Amazon founder Jeff Bezos addressed the news last year by asking followers on X, "Who'd you pick as the next Bond?"

(MGM) Sean Bean in "GoldenEye."

 (MGM) A few months after Amazon MGM Studios' takeover, Villeneuve was tapped to direct the film. His Bond movie will follow his epic sci-fi sequel, "Dune: Part Three," which opens Dec. 18.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I'm a die-hard Bond fan," Villeneuve previously said. "To me, he's sacred territory. I intend to honor the tradition and open the path for many new missions to come. This is a massive responsibility."
 Steven Knight, writer of "Eastern Promises" and creator of the British TV series "Peaky Blinders," is writing the screenplay.
